reuse.why: Most actions share getMonthWideCategories and reuse existing tag, spreadsheet, mutation and undo helpers, but copyPreviousMonth implements eligibility separately.

duplication.why: Category selection and average-action orchestration are consolidated, but the month-wide eligibility policy remains duplicated between getMonthWideCategories and copyPreviousMonth.

placement.why: Budget policy stays in the server budget actions module, tag parsing uses the shared utility, and method registration follows the existing application layer.

scope.why: The edits are confined to the requested month-wide actions, their registration, a focused test and release notes.

maintainability.why: The shared selection helper improves ownership, but maintaining equivalent SQL and imperative eligibility rules makes future policy changes unnecessarily fragile.

bypasses_abstraction.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/budget/actions.ts: copyPreviousMonth bypasses the getMonthWideCategories abstraction introduced for the other month-wide actions.

disguised_duplication.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/budget/actions.ts: copyPreviousMonth expresses the shared eligibility policy as early returns, while getMonthWideCategories expresses it through SQL and filters; saved-template detection is repeated as hasSavedTemplates and NO_TEMPLATE_SQL.

abstraction_drift.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/budget/actions.ts: getMonthWideCategories gains includeHiddenCategories and its conditional hidden-category SQL clause, while copyPreviousMonth independently maintains the same policy.
